B.depoimento: Ordered the construction of 2 spearmen in Barcelona to grow our forces. Sent a detachment of 3 spearmen and 2 archers to assault Tarragona, leveraging the counter triangle advantage against their knight garrison.
B.plano: Build 2 spearmen in Barcelona to reinforce the garrison. Send 3 spearmen and 2 archers to capture Tarragona (21), using the spearman vs knight counter bonus to secure the village with minimal losses. Keep the remaining troops in Barcelona for defense.

A.depoimento: I have ordered my armies to attack Santarem and Evora while my smiths forge 3 new archers. My forces will conquer these villages to expand my territory and bring glory to the kingdom.
A.plano: My campaign aims to rapidly expand by capturing the neutral villages of Santarem and Evora this turn. Next turn, I will build archers at all my villages and send explorers to Coimbra, Badajoz, and Faro to map enemy positions. I will then focus on conquering neutral and enemy villages to reach the goal of 18 villages. I will prioritize building archers and knights for a strong offensive force.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of a knight in Barcelona and dispatched archers to take Girona and Castellon. These neutral villages will expand my domain and provide resources to fund further campaigns.
B.plano: Capture Girona and Castellon using archers to counter the spearman defenders. Build a knight in Barcelona to increase offensive power. Prepare for the assault on Zaragoza next turn by consolidating troops in Tarragona.

B.depoimento: I have launched a multi-pronged assault on the neutral villages. Tarragona's forces are taking Zaragoza, while Barcelona's mighty spearman and knight contingent marches to Girona to prepare for the push on Huesca. I am also reinforcing Tarragona with Castellon's archers and building new units to sustain the momentum.
B.plano: Capture Zaragoza with Tarragona's spearman and archer. Send Barcelona's spearman and knight to Girona to prepare for Huesca. Move Castellon's archers to Tarragona for defense. Build a knight in Barcelona and an archer in Tarragona.

B.depoimento: I attack Huesca and Zaragoza simultaneously to expand my territory. Girona's main force takes Huesca, while Tarragona's archers capture Zaragoza. I am building troops to replace losses and prepare for the next phase.
B.plano: Conquer Huesca with Girona's spearmen, archers, and knights, leaving 2 knights to defend Girona. Conquer Zaragoza with Tarragona's archers, expecting to lose them all. Send Barcelona's knight to Tarragona. Build archers everywhere and a knight in Tarragona to rebuild the army for the next turn.

A.depoimento:
The king's army marches on Coimbra to claim the neutral territory.
We are building more forces for the campaigns ahead.
A.plano: Build archers in Santarem, spearman in Evora and Lisboa. Next turn, attack Coimbra with all Santarem troops and Faro with Evora's spearman. Then push to Badajoz with Lisboa's spearman. Goal: capture neutral villages to reach 18.

B.depoimento: I'm hurling everything I have at Madrid this turn — Tarragona's two knights and Huesca's entire army of four spearmen, two archers and two knights, both columns arriving on turn 7 to crush the four-archer garrison. While they march I'm building two archers in Barcelona, Tarragona and Castellon and a knight in Girona, so the army keeps growing. If this works I'll have seven villages and a real foothold in the centre of the map.
B.plano: Both columns reach Madrid on turn 7: Tarragona's 2 knights (12 effective vs 10, knight counters archer) and Huesca's 4 spear/2 arch/2 knight (16 vs 10) — Madrid falls either way. Builds: 2 archers in Barcelona, Tarragona, Castellon; 1 knight in Girona. Next turn: build 1 archer each in Zaragoza and Huesca (new resources), then push west to Salamanca [7] or Burgos [14]. Keep Girona's 3 knights as a fast strike group. Do not attack Valencia yet.

A.depoimento: King A orders a three-front assault. Our armies march on Badajoz, Faro, and Salamanca simultaneously. We build knights in our cities to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
A.plano: This turn we attack three neutral villages simultaneously. Lisboa's spearmen and archers take Badajoz, Evora's forces take Faro, and Coimbra's knights strike Salamanca. Santarem's archers reinforce Coimbra. We build knights in Lisboa, Santarem, and Evora to have fast mobile forces for the next phase. After capturing these, we will have 7 villages. Next, we will push east from Salamanca towards Madrid and from Badajoz towards Toledo, and capture Porto from Coimbra. Our goal is to reach 18 villages.

B.depoimento: Our archers are on the march to Madrid, where they will join the Huesca army to create a formidable force. Together, we will strike west and claim Salamanca and Burgos for ourselves. The enemy will not know what hits them. Our villages are producing troops without pause.
B.plano: Concentrating all archers in Madrid for the upcoming assault. Next turn, the Huesca army arrives, and we will attack Salamanca with knights and Burgos with archers. Girona's knights remain as a fast strike group. Continue building spearmen and archers for the next phase. Do not attack Valencia yet.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launch a coordinated offensive on three fronts to secure our borders and expand our empire. Our Lisboa army captures Badajoz, while reinforcements from Santarem, Evora, and Salamanca secure the newly conquered hub. Coimbra's forces strike and capture Porto, while Faro's army marches on Sevilha. We also focus on building knights and spearman to replenish our ranks and prepare for the next phase of our campaign towards Madrid and the unexplored eastern territories.
A.plano: Our campaign this turn focuses on capturing three neutral villages to expand our territory and reach the 18-village threshold. The army from Lisboa (already marching) will take Badajoz. We reinforce Badajoz with troops from Santarem, Evora, Salamanca, and Lisboa's remaining forces to secure it as a major hub. Coimbra's army will attack and capture Porto, opening the path north. Faro's army will march on Sevilha to capture it and expand south. We build knights in Lisboa and Evora, spearman in Santarem, and an archer in Coimbra to maintain our military strength. Once we hold these 9 villages, we

B.depoimento: We launched a coordinated double strike from Madrid, sending knights to crush Salamanca and archers to conquer Burgos. Our central army remains strong to defend the capital. The construction of troops across our empire continues at full pace as we expand our territory.
B.plano: Salamanca and Burgos attacked with available troops. Next turn, the reinforcements from other villages will arrive in Madrid, allowing us to attack Toledo and reinforce the newly conquered villages. Keep building troops in all villages. Girona's knights remain as a fast strike group. Do not attack Valencia yet.

A.depoimento: This turn, we launched a strong attack on Salamanca from Badajoz to reclaim the enemy-held village. We reinforced Coimbra and sent a knight to Sevilha to support our conquests. Our builds focus on producing spearman and knights to sustain our offensive.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing Salamanca to secure our northern border. We attack from Badajoz with spearman and archers, leaving knights for defense. We reinforce Coimbra against enemy counterattacks and send a knight to Sevilha. Next, we will target Toledo and Vigo, then push into the enemy heartland. We are building spearman and knights to maintain our army.

B.depoimento: This turn, I am launching a coordinated strike to expand my territory. Madrid's archers are marching to capture the neutral village of Toledo, while Salamanca's knights and archers are rushing to conquer the weak enemy garrison at Coimbra. At the same time, I am reinforcing my border at Salamanca and building knights across my realm to prepare for the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Capture Toledo with Madrid's archers and Coimbra with Salamanca's troops. Reinforce Salamanca with Madrid's spearman. Build knights in all capable villages to build a fast strike force. Next turn, evaluate the situation and prepare to attack Porto or other neutrals with proper counter troops.

A.depoimento: We launched a decisive assault on Salamanca, sending our elite knights from Badajoz to spearhead the attack. Reinforcements from Coimbra march to support the vanguard, while our border villages rotate troops to maintain a strong defense. We are poised to break the enemy's northern front and expand our territory.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing Salamanca to secure our northern border and open the path to Madrid. We attack with knights from Badajoz, supported by the marching army and reinforcements from Coimbra. We rotate our forces, sending knights from Santarem and Evora, and spearmen from Faro to reinforce Badajoz. Next, we will push into the enemy heartland, targeting Toledo and the neutrals in the south.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the assault on Madrid with the full might of Salamanca's knights. Reinforcements are streaming to Badajoz to prepare for the next push into Toledo. Our army is on the move, and the enemy will not be able to stop our advance.
A.plano: Our campaign captures Madrid this turn with Salamanca's knights, then pushes into the enemy heartland. Next turn, we attack Toledo from Badajoz with gathered knights, securing the northern front. We'll then explore and expand north/east from Madrid and Toledo, targeting Burgos, Zaragoza, and beyond. In the south, we prepare to take Cordoba from Sevilha once we have enough archers. Our goal is rapid expansion to 18 villages.

B.depoimento: We launched a major offensive against the enemy village of Badajoz with a powerful archer stack from Toledo. At the same time, we are reinforcing our border villages of Madrid and Zaragoza to secure our territory and prepare for the next wave of expansion. Our workshops are working at full capacity, producing archers and knights to swell our ranks.
B.plano: We are attacking Badajoz with 9 archers from Toledo to conquer an enemy village and open the path to the south. We are reinforcing Madrid with troops from Zaragoza and Burgos to protect our border from enemy counter-attacks. We are reinforcing Zaragoza with troops from Tarragona, Huesca, and Girona (via Barcelona) to build a strong army for future offensives. We are building a massive number of archers and some knights/spearmen across all our villages to grow our army. Next turn, we will see the results of the Badajoz attack and the reinforcements, and plan the next attack (possibly Cordoba or

B.depoimento: I have launched a double attack on the neutral villages of Valencia and Teruel, sending the full strength of Castellon and Zaragoza. These villages will fall next turn, expanding my kingdom to 11 villages. Meanwhile, I have fortified my other villages with new troops, preparing for the next phase of expansion into the south.
B.plano: After Valencia and Teruel fall, focus on the south. If Madrid is safe, send Zaragoza's new troops to Madrid, then to Toledo to attack Cordoba. If Madrid is attacked, defend it. Also consider attacking Pamplona from Burgos. Keep building troops.

B.depoimento: The King's armies move on all fronts! Castellon takes Valencia, Huesca takes Pamplona, and Zaragoza's combined host crushes Teruel. In the west, Madrid's finest storm Salamanca, while Burgos rushes to our capital's defense. Barcelona sends its knights to Zaragoza to ready the next strike. The net of our expansion tightens!
B.plano: We are launching a multi-pronged offensive this turn to conquer four neutral/enemy villages: Valencia, Teruel, Pamplona, and Salamanca. Castellon attacks Valencia. Huesca attacks Pamplona. Zaragoza reinforces Teruel (already marching). Madrid attacks Salamanca. Barcelona reinforces Zaragoza for the next push. Burgos reinforces Madrid to defend it after the attack. We are building troops in all villages, focusing on spearmen for defense and knights for offensive power.

A.depoimento: This turn, I sent reinforcements to Coimbra from Lisboa, Santarem, and Porto to bolster its defenses. I also sent a knight from Faro to Badajoz to strengthen that key border village. In all my villages, I ordered the construction of knights and archers to grow my army for the coming battles.
A.plano: Reinforce the northern border villages to defend against enemy attacks. Build troops in all villages to expand the army. Once Coimbra is secured, launch attacks on Salamanca and Toledo to push the enemy back. In the south, prepare to take Cordoba to open the road east and explore unexplored territories to locate the enemy capital and other villages.

B.depoimento: This turn, we launch precise strikes to expand our territory. Toledo sends archers and a knight to conquer Cordoba, while Salamanca's knight captures Coimbra. We reinforce Valencia and Burgos to prepare for the next phase of our campaign, and we continue building spearmen across our villages to secure our borders.
B.plano: We are attacking Cordoba from Toledo with 3 archers and 1 knight, and Coimbra from Salamanca with 1 knight. We are reinforcing Valencia from Teruel and Burgos from Madrid to prepare for the next pushes on Murcia and Pamplona. We are building troops in all our villages, focusing on spearmen for defense.

B.depoimento: King B has ordered his armies to strike at the neutral villages of Pamplona and Vigo, aiming to expand his territory and secure new sources of resources. Reinforcements have been dispatched to Valencia and Salamanca to strengthen our positions for the next phase of the campaign against King A's forces.
B.plano: Attacking Pamplona from Zaragoza and Vigo from Burgos to capture both neutrals. Sent Teruel to Valencia and Madrid to Salamanca to reinforce for next attacks. Next turn, attack Murcia from Valencia and Porto from Vigo. Build knights in all rich villages and spearmen in Valencia/Teruel. Watch for enemy counterattacks on Toledo and Cordoba; if they fall, retake them after securing the neutrals.

A.depoimento: Our armies struck on three fronts! Porto took Vigo, Badajoz captured Toledo, and Sevilha seized Cordoba. Reinforcements flowed from the interior to secure our borders. The enemy's defenses shattered, and we now hold key positions on the road to victory!
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing weakly defended enemy villages to rapidly expand our territory. This turn, we assault Vigo, Toledo, and Cordoba simultaneously. Reinforcements march from the interior to Coimbra and Badajoz, preparing for a push toward Salamanca and Madrid next turns. We will consolidate our gains and build up armies to reach the 18-village threshold.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike simultaneously at multiple fronts! Coimbra's archers and knights assault Salamanca, Toledo's forces divide to take Madrid and Teruel, and Vigo's troops capture Burgos. Reinforcements from the interior pour into the front lines, while our workshops produce new soldiers to maintain the momentum. We are closing in on the enemy!
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing weakly defended enemy villages to rapidly expand our territory. This turn, we assault Salamanca from Coimbra, Madrid and Teruel from Toledo, and Burgos from Vigo. Reinforcements march from the interior to the front lines, and we build troops at key villages to replace losses and prepare for the next push eastward. We aim to reach the 18-village threshold quickly.

B.depoimento: This turn I launched a two-pronged attack: Valencia's spearmen took the neutral Murcia, and Salamanca's knights crushed Porto. I also sent reinforcements to my weak border villages and built troops across my empire. The enemy is on the back foot, and I'm closing in.
B.plano: Take Murcia and Porto to reach 14 villages. Reinforce Teruel, Madrid, and Burgos against enemy counterattacks. Build up reserves for next turn's push on Toledo and Vigo. Do not attack Badajoz or Coimbra yet.

A.depoimento: We have ordered coordinated assaults on Porto, Madrid, and Murcia. Our knights from Coimbra, Salamanca, and Cordoba will strike simultaneously, overwhelming the enemy garrisons. Reinforcements are marching from the interior to the front lines, and we are building new troops to sustain the campaign. We aim to break through the enemy line and expand our territory.
A.plano: We are launching a three-pronged attack to capture Porto, Madrid, and Murcia this turn, bringing our total to 14 villages. We are building troops across our realm to prepare for the next pushes: we will reinforce Toledo from Badajoz to secure the center and prepare to attack Teruel next turn. We will also push east from Madrid and Murcia into unexplored territory to find more enemy villages. Our ultimate goal is to reach 18 villages and hold them.

B.depoimento: This turn, I sent knights from Zaragoza and Huesca to reinforce Madrid against the enemy army marching on our capital. I also launched an attack on Toledo with knights from Teruel, hoping to conquer this weakly defended enemy village. Meanwhile, I ordered new troops to be built across my villages to rebuild my forces and prepare for the next phase of my campaign.
B.plano: Reinforced Madrid with knights from Zaragoza and Huesca to defend against the incoming enemy army. Attacked Toledo with knights from Teruel to conquer it. Built new troops in all villages to replenish forces and prepare for future attacks on Vigo and other targets. Next turn, assess the battles in Madrid and Toledo, and plan the push on Vigo.

A.depoimento: Our armies are on the move! We are concentrating our forces on the borders to launch a decisive offensive. This turn, we strike at Teruel, taking the first step towards securing the eastern front. Reinforcements are being trained in our cities to support the campaign.
A.plano: We are moving our major armies to the front lines to prepare for a massive push next turn. Coimbra marches to Salamanca, Badajoz to Toledo, Cordoba to Murcia, and Porto to Vigo. This turn, we will attack Teruel with Toledo's troops to secure a foothold and start capturing enemy territory. We will build knights and archers across our realm to replenish our forces.

A.depoimento: Our armies strike on three fronts this turn! Toledo's knights charge against Madrid, Murcia's archers overwhelm Valencia, and Teruel's fast troops capture Zaragoza. Reinforcements flow to our border villages to hold the line, and we build more knights and archers to keep the momentum. The path to 18 villages is within reach!
A.plano: Attack Zaragoza from Teruel with fast troops, Valencia from Murcia with full army, and Madrid from Toledo with all forces. Reinforce Salamanca from Coimbra, Toledo from Cordoba/Badajoz, and Vigo from Porto. Build knights and archers everywhere to replenish. Next turn, with 17 villages, we push on Burgos to reach 18 and hold for victory.

B.depoimento: King B has ordered a full mobilization of his army. All available troops are marching to the borders, with the vanguard striking at Teruel. I have also ordered the construction of knights in all my villages to swell my ranks. The enemy will soon find themselves surrounded by a tide of steel and spear.
B.plano: I am mobilizing all my available troops to the border villages, concentrating them in Castellon and Zaragoza. The main attack will be from Castellon to Teruel (6 spearman, 3 knight), which should easily overcome its defense of 10. I am building 2 knights in every village to grow my army for the next turns. My goal is to conquer Teruel first, then push towards Toledo and the south.

A.depoimento: King A orders the full might of Valencia upon Teruel and Vigo upon Burgos. Our archers will sweep the enemy spearmen, and our knights will shatter their lines. The enemy cannot stand before our wrath. We march to conquer and secure our empire's future!
A.plano: We are launching a double offensive this turn to conquer Teruel and Burgos, bringing our total to 17 villages. Valencia sends its entire garrison (3 spear, 7 arch, 5 knight) to Teruel, leveraging the archer counter for an overwhelming force. Vigo sends its entire garrison (8 arch, 6 knight) to Burgos, also using the archer counter to crush the defense. We are building extensively across all our villages to reinforce our borders and prepare for the next push to Zaragoza or other enemy territories to reach the 18-village threshold.

B.depoimento: King B's forces strike simultaneously at Toledo, Madrid, and Valencia, exploiting the enemy's weaknesses with the counter triangle. In the north, Pamplona's knights march to Burgos to prepare for the assault on Vigo. The kingdom's borders expand!
B.plano: Launch a three-pronged attack on Toledo, Madrid, and Valencia using counter-troop matchups to minimize losses. Send knights from Pamplona to Burgos to reinforce them for the Vigo attack next turn. Keep building knights and archers in all villages to maintain growth.

A.depoimento: We have mobilized the entire kingdom! The armies of the rear are marching to the front to join the great assault. Salamanca, Teruel, and Burgos have launched their attacks on Madrid, Zaragoza, and Pamplona respectively. The fate of the realm hangs in the balance, but our swords are sharp and our courage is high!
A.plano: Our campaign this turn focuses on a massive multi-front offensive to capture three key enemy villages: Madrid, Zaragoza, and Pamplona. By concentrating our forces from the rear interior villages to the front lines, we will overwhelm the enemy defenses. Salamanca will lead the assault on Madrid, Teruel on Zaragoza, and Burgos on Pamplona. Capturing these three villages will bring our total to 18, putting us on the path to victory. In the coming turns, we will consolidate our new territories and push further into enemy lands.

A.depoimento: This turn, I am ordering a massive reinforcement of Zaragoza with troops from Madrid, Pamplona, and Teruel. I am also building knights at Madrid and Pamplona, and spearmen at Toledo, Salamanca, and Teruel to prepare for the next push into enemy territory. Reinforcements from the interior are marching to the front lines.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing Zaragoza next turn with overwhelming force from Teruel, Madrid, and Pamplona. After taking it, we will push north to Huesca and east to Tarragona/Barcelona. We are building up our front-line villages and consolidating our new territories. The goal is to reach 18 villages and hold them for 2 consecutive turns to win.

B.depoimento: Today, we stand firm! While the enemy marches on Zaragoza, we reinforce our defenses there to ensure they meet a bloody end. At the same time, our forces from Valencia and Castellon strike swiftly at Teruel, aiming to crush the enemy and expand our glorious kingdom. We build tirelessly, ready to unleash our knights upon the archers of King A!
B.plano: Reinforce Zaragoza from Tarragona and Huesca to hold off the enemy army marching there. Simultaneously, launch a double attack from Valencia and Castellon to conquer the weakly defended Teruel. Build 2 knights and 1 archer in every village to maximize our offensive power and prepare for the next phase of the campaign.

A.depoimento: We launched a decisive double assault on Valencia and Huesca this turn, aiming to crush the enemy's borders. Our forces in Murcia and Zaragoza moved swiftly, while reinforcements arrived at our key front-line villages to secure our holdings. We are on track to hold our 18 villages and push towards total victory.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on eliminating the enemy's weak border villages to secure our hold on 18 villages and push towards total victory. This turn, we launch a two-pronged attack: from Murcia to Valencia and from Zaragoza to Huesca. We reinforce Teruel and Zaragoza to prepare for the next phase of the campaign, aiming to consolidate our front and move towards Barcelona.

B.depoimento: This turn, we strike at Pamplona with a swift knight-led force, exploiting the enemy's archer-heavy garrison. We reinforce our eastern borders by sending troops to Castellon and Huesca. Our builds focus on archers and spearmen to bolster our ranks. The Teruel campaign continues with the marching army, though heavy losses are expected. We aim to expand our territory and move closer to victory.
B.plano: Attack Pamplona from Huesca with knights and archers to conquer a weakly defended village. Reinforce Castellon from Tarragona and Huesca from Girona to protect our borders. Build archers and spearmen in all villages to increase our army. The army marching to Teruel is likely lost; we focus on easier targets. Next turn, we will assess the situation and prepare to attack Burgos from Pamplona.

A.depoimento: We launched all-out attacks on Pamplona and Castellon, crushing the enemy's defenses and conquering both villages. In a bold move, we emptied our border villages of Zaragoza and Teruel to achieve overwhelming victories, while marching huge reinforcements from the rear to secure our new territories and prepare for the final push towards Barcelona.
A.plano: Our campaign focuses on eliminating the enemy's border villages to secure total victory. This turn, we launch a decisive double attack: from Zaragoza to Pamplona and from Teruel to Castellon, using all available troops to overwhelm the enemy garrisons. We sacrifice these border villages temporarily, marching massive reinforcements from the rear (Salamanca, Madrid, Toledo, Murcia) to fill the gaps and establish a new, unbreakable front line. Our goal is to conquer the remaining enemy villages (Tarragona, Girona, Barcelona) in the following turns.

B.depoimento: This turn, we struck on three fronts: our forces from Pamplona took the empty Burgos, while our armies from Girona and Castellon assaulted Huesca and Valencia respectively. We moved the Barcelona garrison to strengthen Tarragona against the enemy's heartland. Our smithies forged new spearmen, archers, and knights to fill our ranks. We pray these bold moves bring us closer to holding 18 villages.
B.plano: We launched attacks on Burgos, Huesca, and Valencia to expand our territory, and reinforced Tarragona from Barcelona. We built new troops in all villages to replenish our forces. Next turn, we must assess the battle results and watch for enemy counterattacks on Pamplona, Girona, and Castellon, which we left with small garrisons. If we lost any villages, we will need to retake them. We will also plan the next phase of expansion, possibly targeting Toledo or other weak villages.
